title: add live-edit RAG playground with webhook tool-mocks and telemetry probes
author: Maya Patel
description: Summary: This PR introduces a new lightweight, live-edit RAG playground focused on developer feedback loops: editable prompt templates, webhook-based tool mocking, a step-through execution view, and telemetry probes for latency/cost annotation. Motivation: teams building retrieval-augmented features need a local iterate-and-debug experience that mirrors production tool-calling (webhooks, functions) and lets them validate prompt-driven regressions with deterministic mocks and inline assertions. The playground fills the gap between small quickstarts and full production examples by being small, runnable in a devcontainer, and instrumented for unit-style checks and telemetry. What’s included: - A react-based live editor UI (playground) that persists sessions locally and streams incremental LLM output. - A minimal webhook-mock server (Python/Flask) that can emulate common external tools (search, file-store, code-exec), configurable with deterministic fixtures. - A stepper pane showing the RAG pipeline: retrieval hits, prompt composition, tool calls, and final generation with token-level timing annotations. - Telemetry probes and example SDK hooks that emit synthetic latency/cost tags so developers can see per-step unit economics. - A small test harness with example assertions and replay fixtures to reproduce regressions. - Devcontainer + Makefile + CI smoke test to run the mock server and basic e2e in headless mode. Usage notes: - Quickstart: git clone && cd redwood-examples/live-edit-playground && make dev -> opens localhost:3000 and starts webhook mock on :5000. - Fixtures live in ./fixtures and are easy to map to Linear tickets for reproducible bug reports. - Environment variables documented in README; secrets are not required for the mock mode. Checklist: - [x] Playground UI with editable prompt templates - [x] Webhook-mock server and fixtures - [x] Stepper and telemetry probes - [x] Devcontainer and CI smoke test - [x] Docs/README with usage and troubleshooting Non-goals: This is not a production-ready orchestration; it intentionally uses deterministic, in-memory mocks and does not attempt to replicate Redwood Dedicated autoscaling or private installer flows. Related work: ENG-2145 (RAG dev feedback loop), PM-639 (developer productivity OKR). Post-merge follow-ups: - Add more fixtures for vector DB edge-cases (ENG-2201) - Wire the telemetry probes into Redwood Console example dashboards (ENG-2259)
